correctness.rationale: For each \(\sigma>0\), \(F'(q)=p(0)-p(1)\in(0,1)\) proves a unique fixed point. Integrating logistic probability and solving the positive root of \(az^2+(r-1)z-r=0\) derives the exact \(\operatorname{arsinh}\) formula. The noiseless \(\delta=0\) best-response threshold has every mass in \([0,1]\). The limits follow by uniform elementary logarithmic asymptotics, including the transition at exponent one and sharpened error terms. The standalone standard-library numerical checker passed 20 balance-root tests, nine independent quadratures and nine small-noise correction/reflection checks; finite tests do not replace proof.

value.rationale: A primary recent congestion-game work explicitly provides a continuum of equilibria outside its uniqueness hypothesis. In that motivated degeneracy, the exact calculation identifies whether noise selects a robust equilibrium: an arbitrarily small external cost offset, exponentially small in the noise, can select any equilibrium mass. This is a complete singular-selection classification with a natural rate variable, not a routine one-off numeric improvement. It matters for interpreting zero-noise regularization and equilibrium-selection sensitivity in positive-feedback routing or participation models.
